data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, the name Baruch means ‘blessed’ or ‘God is my light.’ In the Bible, Baruch is the name of a scribe who lived in Jerusalem during the Babylonian exile and wrote a letter of encouragement to the Jewish exiles in 515 BC. He is considered a minor prophet in the Old Testament. The name Baruch carries the meaning “Blessed by God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Baruch usually hope their child will grow to embody blessed by god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Baruch total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_english.name: Baruch
in_english.meaning: blessed, blessed one, son of God, blessed by God
in_english.long_meaning: Baruch is a Hebrew name meaning 'blessed', derived from the root בָּרָךְ, meaning 'to bless' or 'to praise'. In the Bible, Baruch is the name of a scribe who is a relative of Jeremiah (Jeremiah 32:12, 43:3). He is also the name of a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church, known for his faithfulness and obedience to God. The name Baruch has been used throughout Christian history to signify one who is blessed by God, and has been a popular name for boys in many Christian cultures.

data.cultural_impact: The name Baruch has a rich historical and cultural impact in Jewish and Christian traditions. In Jewish culture, the name has been in use since Biblical times, and it continues to be popular today. In Christian culture, the name Baruch has a special significance due to the presence of the scribe Baruch in the Old Testament and the story of his encouragement to Jewish exiles, which can be seen as a metaphor for hope and resilience in difficult times.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Baruch carries a deep spiritual significance, as it reminds us that God is the source of all blessings in our lives. The name implores the divine presence and blessings, and it serves as a constant reminder of the importance of maintaining a strong spiritual connection with the Almighty. As it is written in the Bible, "Blessed is the one who trusts in the Lord, who depends on his steadfast love." (Jeremiah 17:7) By bearing the name Baruch, one is affirmed to carry the blessings of God and to share them with others.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Baruch means "blessed" in Hebrew, and in the Bible, Baruch was the scribe and friend of the prophet Jeremiah. In Christianity, the name Baruch symbolizes one who is deeply devoted to God and blessed with His grace and favor.

biblical_reference.note: Baruch is a scribe who is a relative of Jeremiah

historical_references.reference: Baruch was a scribe in the court of King Jehoiakim of Judah during the Babylonian captivity. He is considered the author of the Book of Baruch, which is included in some editions of the Old Testament as an apocryphal text.

Baruch was a disciple and companion of the Apostle John. He is traditionally identified as the author of the Epistle of Baruch, which is included in some versions of the New Testament as a part of the deuterocanonical books.
